messages:
noah: quick flag — security ran a collision check on pseudonym tokens and found a tiny number of collisions between different plaintext inputs. not huge but it's a risk.
ops-bot: alert: pseudonym.collision_check route=/v1/chat collisions=4 scan_window=30d :warning:
sana: details? how many bits are we truncating to currently?
noah: current token = hmac_sha256(tenant_key, value)[:12] (12 hex chars = 48 bits). collisions observed in 30d scan across 10M tokens ~ 4 collisions.
mia: 48 bits is pretty small for long-lived identifiers. we should increase to 32 hex (128 bits) to be safe.
leo: agree. ops/console impact: this is a rollout risk. existing tokens in telemetry will stay same. new tokens must use versioned token format like `P1:<old>` -> `P2:<new>` so we can tell them apart.
sana: migration problem: we don't store raw values (by design). we can't recompute new tokens for old rows unless we have raw. so approach: 1) bump token version for new pseudonyms, 2) run a background re-token job only for quarantined samples that still have raw (rare), 3) treat collisions as separate tokens if same token appears across tenants — collision metric flagged.
noah: operational proposals: - increase truncated length to 32 hex; - add token version prefix v2; - add metric `inspect.pseudonym_collision_rate`; - add alert if collision_rate > 0.0001% per million.
mia: security note: ensure tenant_key includes tenant+version salt and KMS envelope. KMS rotation must be safe: old keys still verify old tokens, new tokens use new keys. add key versioning scheme.
leo: console UX: ops need a "Re-tokenize quarantined samples" action that runs a secure job (RBAC, audit) only on samples that still have raw attachments. also need a read-only panel listing collisions (token, count, sample ids masked).
sana: legal: storing a mapping old_token->new_token might be considered processing of identifiers. we should avoid keeping mappings that allow reversible linking. prefer token versioning without mapping.
legal: correct — don't store mappings that could be used to re-identify. If you need to re-tokenize, do it only on raw data and write the new token; then immediately drop the raw. Keep audit events but not mapping tables. We'll review RFC.
noah: short-term mitigation: 1) raise token length to 24 hex (96 bits) immediately behind a feature flag; 2) enable collision alert and sampling of raw hashed fingerprints at 1-in-10000 for forensics (only for security/ops).
mia: sampling raw even 1-in-10000 requires extra legal sign-off. prefer 1-in-100000 if possible.
leo: rollout plan: feature flag + console indicator -> deploy to canary -> monitor collision metric for 48h -> promote. Re-tokenization job is separate RFC.
sana: tests: add unit collision-probability test, property test to assert token uniqueness under heavy synthetic inputs, integration to ensure new `v2` tokens do not collide with `v1` in our sample window.
ops-bot: added feature flag inspect.pseudonym_version state=rolling target=canary user=noah ts=5976543238 :white_check_mark:
noah: I'll open RFC with specifics: token format, key versioning, KMS rotation, console action, metrics, and legal review items. target PR tomorrow.
legal: please include data retention/DSAR implications and the exact sampled-forensics plan.
mia: also add a dashboard panel `inspect.pseudonym_collision_rate` and histogram of token lengths by tenant.
leo: for immediate incident response, I'll add a readonly collision list in the ops console and block any debug headers that allow raw capture until we confirm new token length.
sana: thanks. low-risk but important. closing once RFC + canary pass. :thumbsup:
